target_state: FUN_006413d0 is a 43-byte, 17-instruction, single-basic-block wrapper. It takes its receiver in ECX, aliases it into ESI, and makes three virtual calls on that same receiver through the receiver's own dispatch word, at table displacements 0xa4, 0xa8 and 0xac, handing the first and the third a single literal-zero stack word and the second nothing at all. It restores ESI and returns through a bare RET, so its own return value is whatever the third call left in EAX. There is no branch of any kind, no global, no local, and no store to the receiver. The machine record classifies it as a leaf with zero direct callees and three indirect transfers, and the eight vtable records that reference its address are consistent with it being a per-class virtual method that forwards to three sibling virtual methods of its own class.

implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX only; NO ordinary stack arguments. The prologue is PUSH ESI / MOV ESI,ECX (0x006413d0, 0x006413d1) and the epilogue is POP ESI / RET (0x006413f9, 0x006413fa), with no SUB ESP and no ADD ESP anywhere, so ESP is balanced on entry and exit and the terminator's bare C3 leaves the caller owning the cleanup of an empty argument area. The receiver is read through ESI at its displacement 0x00 three times (0x006413d3, 0x006413df, 0x006413eb) and is handed back in ECX explicitly at 0x006413e7 and 0x006413f5. The first transfer does not re-establish ECX because nothing between 0x006413d0 and 0x006413dd writes ECX: the two loads and the PUSH do not touch it, so the ECX that callee sees is the entry ECX, which is the same receiver. Ghidra's own prototype for this VA is `undefined FUN_006413d0(void)` with parameter_count 0, which agrees on the empty argument area and says nothing else.
implementation.return_type_basis: The bare C3 rules out a hidden return pointer: a function returning a non-trivial class by value on x86-32 MSVC pops that pointer with `RET 4`, and there is no immediate here. So the result travels in EAX. EAX is written exactly once after the last transfer, by the CALL at 0x006413f7; 0x006413f9 is POP ESI and 0x006413fa is RET, so nothing disturbs it. The model therefore returns the third transfer's return word and nothing else, and the returns of the transfers at 0xa4 and 0xa8 are dead. The machine record's own classification of EAX is register_class aggregate_unknown with return_semantics unclassified_in_EAX, and ghidra_function.return_type is `undefined`: both are consistent with a bare EAX pass-through and neither settles whether the third callee returns a scalar or nothing. That is why the declared type is the model's choice, stated as such, rather than a claim about the callee.
implementation.receiver_model: one named member, at the only displacement the body reads: the dispatch word at +0x00 (`8B 06` at 0x006413d3, 0x006413df and 0x006413eb). Everything past it is an opaque byte run. The machine record agrees exactly (receiver register ECX, offsets [0], shape R-ALIAS, written_through 0, slot-0 write present false). The modelled size is 0x10 bytes, which is a MODEL CHOICE with a hard lower bound of 0x04 and no upper bound: nothing in this body reads or writes past the leading word, and 0x10 exists so the model test has somewhere to put the neighbouring-offset decoys at +0x04/+0x08/+0x0c.
implementation.dispatch_model: three register-indirect transfers, each of the form: one dword load out of the receiver (`8B 06`) into EAX, one dword load at a displacement of EAX (`8B 90 dd dd dd dd`) into EDX, and `FF D2`. That is ONE level of indirection through the receiver followed by a 4-byte-stride read -- not a table of tables, not a second dereference, and not a scaled index. The three displacements are 0xa4, 0xa8 and 0xac. The receiver word is RE-LOADED for every transfer (three separate `8B 06`), which is a real machine property and not style: a callee that replaces the receiver's dispatch word is seen by the next transfer, and the model reproduces that by re-reading through `load_dispatch_table` at each of the three sites. The model test drives exactly that with a first-transfer callee that overwrites the leading word.
implementation.dependency_note: there is no direct callee in this body. All three transfers are register-indirect (`FF D2` through EDX) and the machine record agrees: `callees` is empty, `ghidra_function.callees` is empty, `abi_derived.dispatch` records indirect_calls 3 with call_offsets [] and the target's classification is `leaf`. The three externs in the package header are therefore the seams the package's own model test fills, one per call site, not the callees of a real object. The per-class target addresses are NOT constants of this body: the table at 0x013ff648 holds 0x00641cd0 / 0x00641e10 / 0x00641e40 at the three displacements, and the seven other recorded tables give fifteen further different values at the same three displacements, so the model dispatches through the receiver's own table and never through a fixed address. Nothing about those three functions' bodies is reconstructed or asserted here.

observed_original_abi.receiver_alias: ESI, by 0x006413d1 MOV ESI,ECX. Every receiver access in the body is through ESI; ECX is then reused as the argument register of the second and third transfers (the two `8B CE` at 0x006413e7 and 0x006413f5), which is why the machine record reports ECX with shape R-ALIAS.
observed_original_abi.frame: entry-4 is the saved ESI, pushed at 0x006413d0 and popped at 0x006413f9. There is no SUB ESP and no local, so the frame is four bytes and nothing else. The PUSH 0x0 at 0x006413db writes entry-8 and the PUSH 0x0 at 0x006413f3 writes entry-8 again once the first callee has consumed its word. `PUSH imm8` sign-extends to a full 4-byte push, so the argument really is a 4-byte zero on the stack.
observed_original_abi.stack_discipline_proof: If any of the three callees failed to consume its own pushed word, the POP ESI at 0x006413f9 would pop that word instead of the saved ESI and the C3 at 0x006413fa would return to the wrong address. The body therefore only balances if all three callees are callee-cleaned, which is an independent check on their conventions.
observed_original_abi.exception_frame: none. No FS:[0] write, no try-level word, no handler.
observed_original_abi.ghidra_convention_note: ghidra_has_calling_convention is false and ghidra_calling_convention is null, with the signal recorded as no_information; conventions.calling_convention is INFERRED with corroboration not_available. The listing is followed: the receiver is in ECX at entry, the terminator has no immediate, and the three callees are handed the receiver in ECX. Ghidra's `void` return is not adopted, because EAX demonstrably holds the third call's return word at the RET; adopting void would make the body's last write to EAX unmodelled and untestable.
observed_original_abi.callee_conventions: All three are __thiscall with the receiver in ECX. Two are handed one stack word (the literal 0) and one is handed none, and that is fixed twice over: by this body's own pushes (0x006413db and 0x006413f3 present, nothing before 0x006413e9), and independently by the terminators of the three concrete targets in the table at 0x013ff648 -- 0x00641cd0 ends `83 C4 10 / C2 04 00` (ADD ESP,0x10; RET 4), 0x00641e10 ends `FF 83 C4 08 / 5F 5E C3` (POP EDI; POP ESI; RET, no immediate), and 0x00641e40 ends `5B 83 C4 14 / C2 04 00` (POP EBX; ADD ESP,0x14; RET 4). One word, no word, one word: the three terminators agree with the three call sites one for one, and the middle target is the only one of the three that pops nothing.
observed_original_abi.evidence_level: the 43 bytes are re-read from the image and every ABI fact above is read out of them; the three concrete target terminators are read out of the image at 0x00641cd0, 0x00641e10 and 0x00641e40. The per-class target addresses are recorded as observations, not as constants of this body.

mechanics.body_shape: 17 instructions, 43 bytes, ONE basic block. There is no conditional jump, no unconditional jump, no loop, no switch and no call through a computed address other than the three `FF D2`. Every instruction falls through to the next, and the block ends in the bare RET at 0x006413fa. `ghidra_function.size_bytes` is 43 and `body_span_bytes` is 43, which agrees.

frame_resolution.method: linear ESP walk from entry 0, with the PUSH at 0x006413d0 and the POP at 0x006413f9 as the only frame operations and the bare C3 as the only terminator.
frame_resolution.corroboration: three independent checks agree. (1) The prologue/epilogue are symmetric: PUSH ESI / MOV ESI,ECX and POP ESI / RET, with no SUB ESP and no ADD ESP, so the frame is exactly the four bytes of the saved ESI. (2) The stack-discipline proof above: the body only balances if the three callees consume their own words, and the three terminators in the table at 0x013ff648 do exactly that. (3) The bare C3 with no immediate means the caller never pushed an argument word or a hidden return pointer for this function, so the argument area is empty -- which is the same fact the machine record reports as stack_cleanup_bytes 0 / side caller.

receiver_displacement.0x00: read three times, at 0x006413d3, 0x006413df and 0x006413eb, each as `8B 06` = MOV EAX,[ESI]. The machine record's receiver offsets list is [0] and written_through is 0, which agrees that this is the only receiver word reached and that the body never writes through it.

mechanics.control_flow: linear, single block, 17 of 17 instructions consumed, no branch target inside the body. The three transfers are the only control transfers and all three return to the following instruction.
mechanics.no_store: The body contains no memory-write instruction at all. Its only writes are the two PUSH immediates onto its own frame and the PUSH/POP of ESI; the 17 instructions are otherwise register moves, dword LOADS, and calls. So the receiver must be byte-identical before and after, and the model test asserts that by comparing all 16 receiver bytes across every case.
mechanics.globals: none. No instruction in the body names a data-segment address. Every operand is a register, the immediate 0, or a memory reference through ESI or EAX.

mechanics.dispatch_reads_are_not_cached: 0x006413d3, 0x006413df and 0x006413eb are three separate `8B 06` instructions reading the same word. The body therefore re-reads the receiver's dispatch word before every transfer, and a callee that rewrites it changes where the following transfers go. This is modelled as three independent loads and is the target of refutation case E.
mechanics.return_semantics_machine: EAX, by pass-through of the third transfer. The bare C3 rules out a hidden return pointer, so no 4-byte cleanup is owed and no buffer was supplied; EAX's last write is the CALL at 0x006413f7; 0x006413f9 and 0x006413fa do not touch it. The first two transfers' returns are dead. What the wrapper's own caller does with the word is not visible from inside this body: the eight vtable records are the only inbound references and none of them is a direct call, so there is no call site to read a use out of.
mechanics.receiver_writes: none. The body has no store instruction; see mechanics.no_store. The only writes anywhere in the 43 bytes are the PUSH immediates and the PUSH/POP of ESI.

return_semantics.value: the return word of the transfer at table displacement 0xac, forwarded unchanged. Verified at runtime by the model test: the first two observers return 0xdeadbeef and 0xfeedface while the third returns 0x5a5a1234, and the function returns 0x5a5a1234; the ABI trampoline then finds 0xabcdef01 in EAX after the call when the third observer returns that.
return_semantics.ownership: the value is produced by the third callee and this body neither copies, transforms nor stores it. The body holds no reference to it after the CALL.
return_semantics.lifetime: immediate. The word exists only in EAX from 0x006413f7 to the RET at 0x006413fa; the body's own frame is popped before the return and holds nothing of it.
return_semantics.confidence: the forwarding is CONFIRMED by the listing and by the model test. Whether the third callee returns a meaningful scalar or a dead EAX is NOT settled by this body -- see unresolved_questions.

evidence.vtable_note: The three columns word_0xa4/0xa8/0xac were read out of each of the eight recorded tables for this package, and the displacement column is computed from the recorded xref addresses against the recorded table addresses. Two things follow, and both matter. First, the three targets are NOT constants of this body: the same three displacements resolve to eighteen distinct values across the eight tables, which is what makes this a per-class virtual method forwarding to three sibling virtual methods rather than a fixed three-call function. Second, the slot INDEX of this body is not uniform -- +0x44, +0x50, +0x60, +0xe0 and +0x108 all occur -- so there is no single ordinal to name, and any SDK method name for the three callees would be an invention. Several of the recorded words are not code addresses (0x00e31100, 0x00b7e380, 0x00b5d860 and similar), which is a further reason not to treat any of them as a fixed target. Nothing from this table is modelled as a member of the receiver beyond the single leading dispatch word, and no slot is named anywhere in the package.
evidence.machine_abi_record: The abi blob carried by this target's own record, verbatim where it is decisive: architecture x86-32, calling_convention __thiscall, hidden_this true, hidden_this_register ECX, receiver true, receiver_register ECX, ret_form RET, return_register EAX, return_semantics unclassified_in_EAX, saved_registers [ESI], stack_cleanup_bytes 0, stack_cleanup_owner caller, termination RET. dispatch: indirect_calls 3, call_offsets [], vtable_shaped_loads 0. cleanup evidence 'ret with no immediate, no stack reads', confidence INFERRED, corroboration not_available. conventions.confidence INFERRED, corroboration not_available. completeness CORE_RESOLVED. conflicts []. The one record field this package reads as a limitation rather than as truth is vtable_shaped_loads 0: the three `8B 90 dd dd dd dd` loads ARE a dispatch chain, and the record's stride recogniser evidently did not classify them. The operand forms above are what the model follows, not that field. Note also that the abi blob's own ablated analyses are nested inside its preview field and are not separately quoted here; the 17-instruction listing is the authority for this package.

unresolved_questions: What the three called methods ARE. The displacements 0xa4, 0xa8 and 0xac are fixed, and the targets in the table at 0x013ff648 are 0x00641cd0, 0x00641e10 and 0x00641e40, but this body does not name them, the pack's types list for this VA is empty, sdk_name is null, and the same three displacements resolve to fifteen further different values in the other seven recorded tables. A Sporepedia method name for any of the three would be an invention. This needs the Sporepedia class declaration from the Spore-ModAPI SDK matched against the table at 0x013ff648, which is a different target's job.

Whether the returned EAX is meaningful. The bare RET and the single write to EAX fix the forwarding, but nothing inside this body says whether the 0xac-slot callee returns a scalar its caller wants or a dead EAX. There is no direct caller to read a use out of: the eight inbound references are all vtable slots. Settling it needs either a caller of a reconstructed sibling, or a runtime trace.

Whether the pushed 0 is a null pointer or a false/0 enum, and its width in the callee's own view. The body pushes a full 4-byte zero and never uses it, so the body cannot distinguish a null pointer from a 32-bit zero-valued flag. The callee's own frame read would settle it, and that is a different target's job.

The slot index of this body in its own class's table, and hence of the three callees. The eight recorded tables place 0x006413d0 at +0x44, +0x50, +0x60, +0xe0 and +0x108, and the recorded table addresses look like detected run starts rather than guaranteed vtable heads -- several of the words inside them are not code addresses. Until one table's head is confirmed, no ordinal can be stated and no override can be assumed.

The receiver's real size and what follows its leading word. Only displacement 0x00 is read, so this body contributes no upper bound. The vtable reaches 0xac, which bounds the TABLE and not the object; the object must be at least large enough to hold the leading word, and nothing more is derivable from here.

The class hierarchy. SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI, the binary's vtable detection never ran headless (0 vtable labels), and the eight tables here are recognised only as data references to this body. So 'this is Sporepedia' comes from the brief's subsystem field and the cluster name, not from a class record, and the class of which this is a virtual method is not established by anything in this package.

Nothing here is runtime validated. There is no differential trace and no Wine oracle run for this target, so every claim rests on the 43 bytes plus the read-only supporting bytes cited under evidence.provenance.

validation.compile_gate: clean. Zero diagnostics under -m32 -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror. The header additionally compiles alone in a translation unit that only includes it, and the whole pair also builds and passes under -fPIC. The reconstructed body contains no assembly and no inline assembly; the two inline-assembly blocks are in the model test and are documented in the test header as validated at this gate and at -fPIC, with the reason spelled out (at -O1 and above the compiler's register allocation breaks the two-block stack choreography in the harness, which is a harness property and not a property of the reconstruction).
validation.model_test: 67 named checks over 14 cases, all passing, exit 0. The three indirect call sites are the seams: six observer functions (two per site, so a table can be swapped between transfers or between calls) are planted into the words of the test's own dispatch tables, and each records which function was entered, the receiver it was handed, the argument it was handed, the receiver's dispatch word as found at that instant, its own return value, and the machine's ESP at that instant. What is asserted: three transfers at 0xa4/0xa8/0xac in that order once each; one level of indirection; the dispatch word re-read per transfer; one identical receiver pointer at all three sites; the two argument words are the literal 0; the stack shape is one word, no word, one word, measured differentially against a hand-written 1/0/1 sequence rather than against a literal offset, because a C++ compiler pads a callee-cleaned argument call and a literal offset would be a fact about GCC; the returned word is the third transfer's and leaves the function in EAX; ESP is balanced across the call; and all 16 receiver bytes are unchanged.

mutation_checking.known_limits: M5, M7 and M13 are detected by the process dying rather than by a named check, because a wrong word in the harness's own table is not a callable. The tables' non-target words were deliberately filled with a callable decoy instead of a poison constant to reduce this (which is what turned M1 from a bare crash into 23 named failures), but a decoy planted in a table word that is out of range still cannot be called. This affects diagnosis only, never detection.

validation.wpedantic_note: The model test's own tables' unfilled words are filled with a callable decoy rather than with 0xcccccccc, for the reason in known_limits. The four-byte stride the body reads is checked in both directions: case B fills a window from 0x80 to 0xac with callables so any displacement one word out lands somewhere observable, and case C uses a 0x300-byte table with callables at 0x290/0x2a0/0x2b0 so that treating the imm32 as a dword INDEX and scaling by four is caught too. Both of the receiver-pointer refutations and the pointer-level refutation are driven from case D, which plants real decoy tables at receiver+0x04/+0x08/+0x0c and a decoy table address in the real table's own leading word. The one thing the test deliberately does NOT do is assert a literal ESP offset at any transfer site, for the compiler-padding reason given in validation.model_test; it asserts the offset DIFFERENCE against a hand-written reference sequence instead, after measuring that the two observer shapes allocate the same stack.

expected_reasons.ABI: __thiscall with the receiver in ECX and an EMPTY argument area: the prologue is PUSH ESI / MOV ESI,ECX, the terminator at 0x006413fa is a bare C3 with no immediate, there is no SUB ESP and no ADD ESP anywhere, and the machine record agrees on convention __thiscall, saved_registers [ESI], stack_cleanup_bytes 0 and side caller. The three callee conventions are corroborated independently by the terminators of the three concrete targets in the table at 0x013ff648: RET 4, bare RET, RET 4 -- one word, no word, one word, matching the two PUSH 0x0 instructions and the one site with no push. The model test measures the empty argument area (ESP balanced across a trampolined call) and the per-site stack shape differentially, rather than asserting either as a convention.
expected_reasons.CALLS: There is no direct callee and the model claims none: `callees` is empty, the record's dispatch block reports indirect_calls 3 with call_offsets [], and all three transfers are FF D2 through EDX. The model reproduces exactly three transfers, in order, each once, and the test sees all three. Argument order and arity per site are fixed by the listing (one word, none, one word) and by the callee terminators, and both are asserted.
expected_reasons.GLOBALS: None, and none declared. No instruction in the 43 bytes names a data-segment address; every operand is a register, the immediate 0, or a memory reference through ESI or EAX. The header declares no global and the .cpp defines none.
expected_reasons.FIELDS/OFFSETS: Exactly one receiver displacement exists and the machine record agrees it is the only one: 0x00, read by `8B 06` at 0x006413d3, 0x006413df and 0x006413eb, with receiver offsets [0] and written_through 0. The three table displacements 0xa4, 0xa8 and 0xac are the imm32 of the three `8B 90 dd dd dd dd` instructions. No member is named beyond the leading dispatch word; the rest of the receiver is an opaque run and its 0x10-byte size is labelled a model choice with a 0x04 lower bound. The table's 0xb0 size is labelled as arithmetic on 0xac + 4, a lower bound rather than a measurement. Refutation cases B, C, D and M13 attack the displacement set from four directions.
expected_reasons.CONSTANTS: The only constants in the body are the three displacements 0xa4, 0xa8 and 0xac, the single immediate 0 (PUSH imm8, so a 4-byte zero), and the absent RET immediate. Each is read straight out of the instruction bytes, each is named as a named constant in the header, and each is asserted against its literal value in the test's verify_model_constants plus a static_assert chain. Nothing was invented: no enum, no flag, no index and no magic number appears anywhere in the package.
expected_reasons.CONTROL FLOW: One basic block, 17 of 17 instructions, no conditional or unconditional jump, no loop, no switch, no indirect jump. The single control flow is the straight line of the three transfers. The model's control flow is that straight line and it carries no branch of any kind, and the test asserts the three transfers happen once each in the fixed order (case A, and case M11 shows that inserting a branch the listing does not have is detected).
expected_reasons.VIRTUAL DISPATCH: Three register-indirect transfers, each one dword load out of the receiver into EAX, one dword load at a displacement of EAX into EDX, and FF D2 -- one level of indirection and a 4-byte stride, not a table of tables and not a scaled index. The three displacements are 0xa4, 0xa8 and 0xac, and the per-class target addresses are not treated as constants: the eight recorded tables give eighteen distinct values at the same three displacements, and the model dispatches through whatever the receiver's own table says. The receiver word is re-read before each transfer and the model reproduces that. Refutation: case B (neighbouring displacements), case C (4x scaling), case D (wrong receiver offset and one level too many), case E (cached dispatch word, caught on the identity of the function entered, which is the only observation that separates the two tables), case J (a different table per call).
expected_reasons.RETURN SEMANTICS: EAX, by pass-through of the third transfer, with the first two returns dead. The bare C3 rules out a hidden return pointer; EAX's last write is the CALL at 0x006413f7 and nothing between it and the RET touches EAX. The test drives three different observer return values and asserts the third's and only the third's leaves the function, and the ABI trampoline then reads the same word out of EAX after the call. What the third callee returns is left open and named in unresolved_questions rather than guessed.
expected_reasons.EVIDENCE COVERAGE: Every instruction of the 43 bytes is annotated in the .cpp with its address, and every number in the header is traced to an instruction or labelled as a model choice with its bound. The bytes themselves were re-read from the image for this package and match the committed listing exactly. Everything not fixed by the machine is in unresolved_questions: the three methods' names, the meaningfulness of the returned EAX, the nature of the pushed 0, the slot index, the receiver's size, the class hierarchy, and the absence of any runtime validation.

known_blockers.name: class/struct tag mismatch on DispatchTable
known_blockers.diagnostic: swarm_w1_006413d0_types.hpp:108:1: error: 'DispatchTable' defined as a struct here but previously declared as a class; this is valid, but may result in linker errors under the Microsoft C++ ABI [-Werror,-Wmismatched-tags]
known_blockers.cause: swarm_w1_006413d0_types.hpp line 93 forward-declared the tag with `class` while line 108 defined it with `struct alignas(4)`. Every other mention in the header, the body and the model test is a bare type name, so the tag keyword appeared in exactly two places and they disagreed.
known_blockers.fix: One keyword. Line 93 `class DispatchTable;` -> `struct DispatchTable;`, plus a comment recording why the keyword is `struct`. The definition site is untouched, so the members (a single std::array<Word, 0xb0/4> slot), the layout (sizeof == 0xb0, static_assert untouched) and the meaning (the receiver's leading dispatch word, indexed at byte displacements 0xa4/0xa8/0xac) are all unchanged. `struct` was chosen because the definition is an alignas(4) aggregate like its sibling SporepediaReceiver.
known_blockers.verified: clang++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -m32 compiles the source TU, the test TU, archives them with ar/ranlib and links the static library into /tmp/g_test with zero diagnostics. The header also compiles alone in a TU that only includes it, under both clang++ and g++, and both TUs compile clean at -fPIC.

known_blockers.name: clang++-only SIGSEGV in the model test's calibration asm block, masked by KB1
known_blockers.reported_by: discovered while verifying KB1: once the compile error was gone, the gate linked and the test binary died with SIGSEGV (exit 139). Reproduced against the unmodified package, so it is pre-existing and independent of KB1.
known_blockers.cause: calibrate_observer_frames (model test) contains one inline-asm block that makes TWO indirect CALLs, and its clobber list named only "eax", "ecx", "memory". EDX was therefore assumed live across the block. On i386 PIC a compiler may keep the GOT base in any register the clobber list leaves alone, and the block then reads its second call target out of that register AFTER the first callee has returned. GCC 16 picks EBX and reloads the operands from memory, so the defect is latent there; clang 22 picks EDX, the first observer returns with EDX == 0, and the second `mov 0xe8(%edx),%ecx` faults. GDB at the fault: eip at the asm, edx 0x0, in calibrate_observer_frames <- case_stack_shape_is_one_zero_one_word <- main.
known_blockers.fix: Added "edx" to that one block's clobber list. The block really does destroy EDX, so this states a fact the constraint list was omitting; it constrains register allocation only. No check(), no case, no measurement and no threshold was added, removed or altered, and the block's instruction text is byte-identical.
known_blockers.why_in_scope: This is the second of the four defect classes the contract's section 5 names explicitly (a SEGFAULT under clang++ that g++ survives, from an inline __asm__ probe whose operand allocation differs between the two compilers). It is a source-shape defect in the harness, not a machine-semantics change, and the gate cannot be evaluated at all until the binary runs. Flagged explicitly because it goes beyond the brief's 'change only the tag keyword', which was read as scoping the DispatchTable repair and not as licensing a known-fatal gate failure to stand.
known_blockers.not_changed_on_purpose: The sibling block call_measured also CALLs but was left alone. It reads no operand register after its one call -- %[target] and %[recv] are "m" operands read before `call *%[target]`, and the two instructions after the call only write their early-clobber outputs -- so it never depends on EDX surviving and is already correct. Adding "edx" there was tried and is not free: the block needs three "=&r" outputs and at -O0 with eax/ecx/edx all reserved clang reports 'inline assembly requires more registers than available'. A comment now records the asymmetry and the reason for it.
known_blockers.verified: The clang++ gate now runs the test to completion instead of dying with SIGSEGV; the crash is gone in 20/20 consecutive runs.

known_blockers.status: SUPERSEDED by KB4, which is RESOLVED -- the reasoning below is kept as the record of why this was a real gate failure and why it was not repairable under a contract that forbade touching the assertion
known_blockers.name: clang++-only failure of H4: the differential stack-shape measurement has no discriminating power at -O0
known_blockers.reported_by: promotion gate after KB1 and KB2 were fixed
known_blockers.symptom: /tmp/g_test exits 1 with exactly one failure: 'H4: the reference sequence really does put the middle site at a different depth, so the comparison below can discriminate'. 65 of 65 checks that execute on the normal path run; H4 is the only failure. Deterministic across 20 runs. g++ at the same -O0 is fully green (exit 0, no output).
known_blockers.measurements: frame_skew = 0 under both compilers, so the observer-frame calibration passes. Reference sequence d21/d31: g++ 16/0, clang++ 0/0. Reconstruction d21/d31: g++ 16/0, clang++ 0/0.
known_blockers.cause: Not a defect in the reconstruction. The one-argument site is the only one of the three with no pushed word, and the test measures it DIFFERENTIALLY, on purpose, because a C++ compiler does not turn a one-word __thiscall call into a bare four-byte push. clang -O0 emits `movl $0,(%esp); call; subl $4,%esp` for the callee-cleaned one-word call, and that `subl $4,%esp` exactly cancels the machine's one argument word, so the following no-word `call` lands at the same depth as the earlier one-word `call` and the differential collapses to 0. GCC -O0 instead pads with `sub $0xc,%esp; push $0; call; add $0xc,%esp`, leaving a 16-byte difference. The reconstruction's own three call sites collapse identically, which is why H4 is the check that catches it.
known_blockers.why_not_fixed: H4 is the harness's own discrimination PRECONDITION, and making it non-fatal is weakening an assertion, which the worker contract forbids outright and which directs a worker that finds itself needing it to stop and report instead. The condition is also not repairable from the reference side: the reconstruction's side is 0 as well, so no reference can produce a matching non-zero difference. Rewriting reference_one_zero_one as hand-written asm was considered and rejected -- it would break the very cancellation that makes the differential compiler-agnostic, which is the reason the reference is C++ in the first place.
candidate_resolutions_for_the_owner: Extend the guard the case already has. case_stack_shape_is_one_zero_one_word already skips H4-H6 with an explicit stderr NOTE when frame_skew != 0, and the case comment already records that 'the 1/0/1 push pattern is covered independently of this measurement, by the argument presence and value checks A6, A7, G1 and G2'. Treating 'the reference cannot discriminate' as a second, clang-specific way for that same premise to fail would keep H4 present and evaluated, report it rather than pass it, and leave 63 of 65 checks asserted. This is a judgment call about assertion scope and is the parent's to make, not a worker's.

Move the 1/0/1 argument-shape claim onto a measurement that does not go through a C++ call site's ESP -- e.g. assert the argument PRESENCE and VALUE per site (which A6/A7/G1/G2 already do) and drop the ESP differential on clang only. This is a larger change to the test and would reduce the number of checks that run.
known_blockers.coverage_that_is_not_affected: The machine facts H5 and H6 exist to protect -- one argument word at 0xa4 and at 0xac, none at 0xa8 -- are independently asserted by A6/A7 (argument presence and value) and G1/G2 (the literal 0 at both argument sites), and by the byte-exact body. Nothing about the reconstruction, the three displacements, the 1/0/1 push pattern or the EAX pass-through is in doubt.

known_blockers.name: clang++-only failure of H4: the differential stack-shape measurement has no discriminating power at -O0
known_blockers.reported_by: promotion gate, after KB1 and KB2 were fixed; diagnosed and repaired by rp22
known_blockers.supersedes: KB3, which recorded the same failure as OPEN and declined to fix it because the only fix it could see was to weaken an assertion. The fix below changes the FORM of the assertion and not its substance, and it adds five checks.
known_blockers.old_check: check(ref_second != ref_first, "H4: the reference sequence really does put the middle site at a different depth, so the comparison below can discriminate")
known_blockers.channel: the callee's own entry frame. Three new top-level assembly entry-frame probes (sw1_entry_probe_a4/a8/ac_006413d0) are planted in a DEDICATED table for this one case, so the six existing observers are untouched and every other case behaves exactly as before. Each probe reads %esp and then 4(%esp) as its first two instructions, before it writes a register of its own, and hands the samples to a C-linkage recorder as ordinary cdecl arguments. The probes return with the terminator their own slot has in the machine: `ret $4` for 0xa4 and 0xac (0x00641cd0 and 0x00641e40 both end `C2 04 00`) and a bare `ret` for 0xa8 (0x00641e10 ends `C3`). A fourth block, run_entry_control_zero_word, enters the SAME 0xa8 probe through a bare `call` with a known zero planted in the word the callee will find at [entry+4], and requires the probe to report it.
known_blockers.why_compiler_independent: At a callee's entry the i386 calling convention puts the return address at [ESP] and the first stack argument at [ESP+4]. That is true whichever way the CALLER chose to materialise the argument, and the two toolchains differ exactly there: g++ -O0 -m32 emits `sub $0xc,%esp; push $0x0; call; add $0xc,%esp` and clang emits `movl $0x0,(%esp); call; sub $0x4,%esp`, with the callee's own `ret $4` taking the word in clang's case. The word is at [entry+4] either way, so the reading is the same. The DEPTH is not the same and is no longer what the check reads: measured at -O0 -m32, all three entry ESPs are equal under clang (0xffc6323c, 0xffc6323c, 0xffc6323c) and spread 0/16/0 under g++ (0xffea4c6c, 0xffea4c7c, 0xffea4c6c).
known_blockers.what_the_old_check_asserted_and_where_th: H4 was the harness's own discrimination PRECONDITION: the differential below it compares two differences, and if the reference's middle site sits at the same depth as its first then both differences are zero and the comparison is true of everything. That premise is unsatisfiable on clang and is not repairable from the reference side -- the reconstruction's own three sites collapse identically (measured 16/0 for g++/clang++ in the reference AND in the reconstruction), and writing the reference as hand assembly would give it a difference the compiled body has no way to match. The claim it guarded -- the 1/0/1 argument-count pattern -- is now asserted where the convention puts it. The differential is KEPT, unchanged, as H2/H3/H5/H6, because it says something the entry-frame reading does not: only the middle site pushes nothing, so only a difference between sites can see that one absence at all. H7 was added to assert the two differential comparisons together.
known_blockers.honest_limit: The 'no argument word at 0xa8' half cannot be read off the middle callee's own [ESP+4] either, and the file says so at the check. Both compilers leave site 1's zero in exactly that word -- clang because it reuses one outgoing-argument slot for the one-word and the zero-word call, g++ because the same slot survives its `add $0xc,%esp` -- so the middle probe's reading is 0 under g++ and site 1's own return address under clang, for a CORRECT body. That absence is carried instead by two things that do not go through a call site's ESP: the frozen header's `SlotTargetSecond` type, which is `Word(__thiscall*)(SporepediaReceiver*)` and so has no stack parameter to fill (a body that pushed one would not compile against it), and case M2, which measures the caller's stack pointer on both sides of the whole call and finds them equal. A body that reserves a word for the 0xa8 call and pops it again before returning is indistinguishable from one that does not, through any ABI-visible channel; the 17-instruction listing (no SUB ESP / ADD ESP other than the PUSH ESI / POP ESI pair) and the byte-identical source are the evidence for it.
known_blockers.check_count: 65 -> 71. One check (H4) was replaced by six, and H7 was added. No check was deleted, skipped, inverted or made conditional on the compiler; there is no #ifdef __clang__ anywhere in the file.
known_blockers.case_count: unchanged at 14 cases. The new work is inside the existing case H.

16 of 16 killed under BOTH compilers. The thirteen the previous record named (M1-M13) are all still killed: M1 ASSERT/ASSERT, M2 ASSERT/ASSERT (E6,E7), M3 ASSERT/ASSERT, M4 ASSERT/ASSERT, M5 FAULT/FAULT, M6 ASSERT/ASSERT, M7 FAULT/FAULT, M8 ASSERT/ASSERT (K2), M9 FAULT/ASSERT, M10 ASSERT/ASSERT, M11 ASSERT/ASSERT, M12 FAULT/ASSERT, M13 ASSERT/ASSERT.
